confidence_notes: I ran six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for Cairo prices. The food and drink anchors come from aggregated, crowd-sourced indexes. Numbeo Cairo (Oct 2026) gave about E£250 for an inexpensive meal, about E£94 for a cappuccino and about E£75-78 for a domestic beer. A Numbeo New Cairo listing gave about E£1,350 for a mid-range meal for two. Expatistan, Wise and Expatarrivals gave consistent figures. I converted EGP to USD at roughly E£50 per USD, which is the rate implied by those sources' own conversions. Beer is the least certain food and drink anchor: index figures (about E£75-82) are well below hotel-bar bottled Stella menus (about E£185-230), so I set it between the two for a licensed restaurant serving. Cocktail and wine rely on Expatistan (a downtown club cocktail at about E£286), a local guide (cocktails E£180-500, local wine E£150-300) and a few hotel menus. These are only partly aggregated and mostly undated. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge, not from searching or inspecting listings, so they carry the most uncertainty. The RBA figure (18 Nov 2026, 0.6720 USD per AUD) comes from a search-result summary of the RBA page. I did not open the page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Priced directly from Cairo and Egypt cost-of-living indexes. Accommodation is modelled on typical Cairo budget-to-3-star tourism pricing, comparable to other low-cost North African and Middle Eastern capitals such as Amman and Marrakech.
